title: Rows in a Tree can become misaligned when using word wrapping
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.4.1.stable.official.49a5bc7b6 ### System information Godot v4.4.1.stable - Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) 12 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Intel(R) Xe Graphics (TGL GT2) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz (8 threads) ### Issue description When using word-wrap in cells of a Tree, the tree can render in a way that results in misaligned rows, as depicted here: Effectively it looks like the cells with the word-wrap enabled get their text wrapped correctly, and increase in vertical size. However the other cells on the same row are not increased in size in the same way, or at least the alignment line is not moved according to the new size. Once the user moves the mouse over the Tree control the misalignment is corrected and the table looks like one would expect: The same can be achieved by queueing a redraw. Though, curiously the queue_redraw has to be called with call_deferred for it to work. ### Steps to reproduce Attached is a MRP that demonstrates the issue (and was used to obtain the screenshots in the issue description above). It basically consists of a Tree node to which some TreeItems are added (in the _ready function), once the scene starts the rows are misaligned. Take care not to have the mouse pointer over the Tree control when starting the application as it will redraw the Tree with the correct alignment. I assume this happens because the control gets redrawn when a mouse hovers over it (the cell that is hovered over lights up after all). So I figured calling a queue_redraw would have the same effect and serve as a work-around. Adding a queue_redraw at the end of the _ready function does not help, but a queue_redraw.call_deferred does (see the comment in my example code). I had some trouble making an MRP. I suspect the issue happens when TreeItems are added to the Tree when the Tree control is not (yet) visible. An earlier attempt at an MRP where I included a button that adds text to a cell in an already visible Tree did not result in the same issue; the text was added to the cell and the rows in the Tree control stayed aligned. However, in a larger project where I first noticed this issue I have added the call to queue_redraw.call_deferred() to the item_rect_changed signal as a work-around, instead of the visbility_changed signal. So maybe the issue is not entirely related to visibility of the control. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21384896/MRP.zip)
